name: pdk-python-hl7-etl
instr:
Results from our second lab don't load with the hl7 library in /app. Two of their nightly files and a capture of their MLLP feed are in /data/inbound/. hl7.parse_file and hl7.parse_hl7 fail on them with UnicodeDecodeError, and forcing an encoding garbles names and comments.

Every message names its character set in MSH-18: ASCII, 8859/1 to 8859/9, 8859/15 or UNICODE UTF-8. When parse, parse_batch, parse_file or parse_hl7 get bytes, each message should be decoded in its own set. The encoding argument is only for an empty MSH-18 and for the file and batch header and trailer segments. Any other MSH-18 value raises hl7.ParseException, and bytes that aren't valid in the named set raise UnicodeDecodeError. Names and comments, hex escapes (\X..\) included, should read through the accessors and Message.unescape exactly as the lab typed them, with no control characters. Message.escape should write non-ASCII as hex escapes in the message's set, so it reads back the same.

hl7.mllp.HL7StreamReader, HL7StreamWriter and hl7.client.MLLPClient.send_message should follow MSH-18 too, using their own encoding only when it's empty. We also build replies in code, as the docs show, or with create_ack. A message should always go by what its MSH-18 says at that moment, also after msg["MSH.18"] is changed or segments are appended, and an ack should declare the same MSH-18 as the message it answers.

Messages with an empty MSH-18 have to work exactly as they do now. The tests in /app/tests, make lint
